target.title: fix(groq): keep default Llama agent turns within TPM limit
target.body:
Closes #104783

AI-assisted with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and the live proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a local agent with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` could receive an immediate HTTP 413 for even a one-word prompt on Groq's 12,000 TPM base tier. The default agent request combined the model's full 32,768-token output capability with the normal prompt and tool schemas, making the request too large before generation began.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Groq plugin now keeps the model's 32,768-token output capability metadata while applying a separate 1,024-token default request budget. Normal implicit-budget requests remain tool-capable; only a specifically matched Groq HTTP 413 `Request too large` TPM rejection is retried once without tool fields. Explicit max-token overrides skip this recovery policy. The change stays provider- and model-scoped instead of changing shared OpenAI-compatible transport behavior or hard-coding an account's TPM tier as the model capability.

## User Impact

Default local-agent turns with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` can complete on Groq's base tier instead of failing before generation. Higher-limit organizations retain the normal tool-capable first request, while affected base-tier requests recover transparently. Other Groq models and explicitly budgeted requests are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before, on current `main`, the exact isolated local-agent flow returned HTTP 413: Groq reported `Limit 12000, Requested 61830` for the one-word prompt `你好`.
- After, the same default command first received the narrowly matched HTTP 413, immediately retried without tool fields, and returned HTTP 200 in the same agent attempt. Groq reported 10,071 input tokens and 452 output tokens (10,523 total).
- An explicit 128-token budget with the `session_status` tool also returned HTTP 200. Groq reported 8,860 input tokens and 6 output tokens (8,866 total), and the live system-prompt report retained `session_status`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/groq` — 4 tests passed, including normal tool retention, exact 413 recovery, explicit-budget preservation, and non-recovery for unrelated 400/401/413-context/429 errors.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/groq/index.ts extensions/groq/index.test.ts extensions/groq/openclaw.plugin.json` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Hosted local validation was unavailable on this machine: Blacksmith Testbox was not installed, and direct AWS Crabbox had no usable instance credentials. The focused local fallback and live provider proof above completed successfully; GitHub CI remains the broad validation gate.
